item.title: [LU-20011] lfs mirror: Invalid layout: Incomplete mirror - must go to EOF
item.description:
If a file with a partial PFL layout (i.e. no EOF component) has a mirror added with "lfs mirror extend" it is then impossible to remove the mirror, add a new EOF component, or "lfs mirror split" to return to the original state, receiving the error "lfs mirror: Invalid layout: Incomplete mirror - must go to EOF".

Whatever generates this error should be ignored, and the split or "setstripe --comp-add" command should be allowed to bring the file back into a consistent state.
item.summary: lfs mirror: Invalid layout: Incomplete mirror - must go to EOF

status.description: This issue is being actively worked on at the moment by the assignee.

comments.comment:
If I am not wrong, this error comes from this block:

if (comp->llc_extent.e_start == 0) {
    first_comp = true;
    args->lsa_mirror_count++;
    /* Most checks apply only within one mirror, this is an
     * exception. */
    if (prev && prev->llc_extent.e_end != LUSTRE_EOF) {
        args->lsa_rc = LSE_INCOMPLETE_MIRROR;
        goto out_err;
    }

in llapi_layout_sanity_cb() function.

I think we can add a new argument (e.g lsa_allow_incomplete_mirrors) and bypass this check, thus the split operation will be able to recover the file into a consistent state.

Does this make any sense?

npapakonstantinou, I was going to write that it isn't permitted to change the function signature for llapi_*() functions, but I now see that the lsa_allow_incomplete_mirrors is in struct llapi_layout_sanity_args which appears local to that function.

It is a bit sad that struct llapi_layout_sanity_args is so poorly laid out, with bool intermixed with pointers and ints of various sizes. According to pahole:

struct llapi_layout_sanity_args {
        _Bool                      lsa_incomplete;       /*     0     1 */
        _Bool                      lsa_flr;              /*     1     1 */
        _Bool                      lsa_ondisk;           /*     2     1 */

        /* XXX 1 byte hole, try to pack */

        int                        lsa_rc;               /*     4     4 */
        char *                     fsname;               /*     8     8 */
        uint16_t                   lsa_mirror_count;     /*    16     2 */
        _Bool                      lsa_in_parity;        /*    18     1 */

        /* XXX 5 bytes hole, try to pack */

        uint64_t                   lsa_last_parity_end;  /*    24     8 */

        /* size: 32, cachelines: 1, members: 8 */
        /* sum members: 26, holes: 2, sum holes: 6 */
        /* last cacheline: 32 bytes */
};

If there was any danger that this struct was exposed to userspace, the safest course of action would be to add the new bool in the 1-byte hole.

So you think that we have to set the lsa_allow_incomplete_mirrors flag always to true?

I noticed that about the signatures and I was thinking to do the same trick with 
llapi_layout_v2_sanity() function and have something like that for backward compatibility:

int llapi_layout_v3_sanity(struct llapi_layout *layout, bool incomplete, bool flr, bool allow_incomplete_mirrors, char *fsname);

int llapi_layout_sanity(struct llapi_layout *layout, bool incomplete, bool flr)
{
	return llapi_layout_v3_sanity(layout, incomplete, flr, false, NULL);
}

int llapi_layout_v2_sanity(struct llapi_layout *layout,
			bool incomplete, bool flr, char *fsname)
{
	return llapi_layout_v3_sanity(layout, incomplete, flr, false, fsname);
}

and in mirror_split() in lfs.c we can directly call the llapi_layout_v3_sanity() with allow_incomplete_mirrors true.

It isn't clear for mirror split/delete if the "sanity" of the layout should be checked at all? The file layout already exists and splitting off/deleting the partial mirror isn't making it any worse than exists today. Maybe only the remaining mirror should be checked for sanity?

Since the goal is to remove the problematic mirror and return to the original state, I think that allowing mirror split command to handle those incomplete mirrors, the goal will be achieved.

What do you mean with the remaining mirror should be checked for sanity ? During split operation or other operation?

I mean that it should be OK to split/delete the partial mirror, but if there is data that is not in the partial mirror then it shouldn't be allowed to split/delete the full mirror and leave the partial mirror behind.
